scientific_question: Do adjacent monthly BTCDVOL futures coexist with enough simultaneous ordinary public trading activity to justify a separately governed near-vs-far calendar-spread study that can hedge common DVOL-index movement?

pair_construction.contract_population: Exact valid BTCDVOL monthly futures discovered by the same deterministic Wednesday enumeration and overlap-window metadata rule as lifecycle source gate V0.2.
pair_construction.pair_rule: Sort confirmed contracts by expiration_timestamp and pair adjacent expiries only.

retained_metrics_only: ordinary public trade count per leg within overlap
unique active UTC days per leg within overlap
common active UTC day count per pair
threshold_rationale: Monthly contracts overlap for roughly a week by design. A usable calendar-spread study should therefore recover at least ten independent adjacent-expiry pair clusters, at least three simultaneous active days per qualifying pair, >=40 aggregate common pair-days, and broad coverage across >=6 quarters. These are source adequacy requirements only.
stop_rule: On any failed source gate, stop. Do not widen overlap intervals beyond exact listed coexistence, lower thresholds, skip sparse adjacent pairs, add non-adjacent pairs, or open prices/outcomes under this gate ID.
post_pass_rule: PASS authorizes only a separately frozen pre-Discovery calendar-spread authority.
